extracted.intended_audience: professional mathematicians, geometers, mathematical historians, and trigonometrical surveyors
extracted.subtask_description: Derivation, demonstration, and exposition of theorems about conic sections (reciprocal polars, envelopes, porisms) and related applied-mathematical formulae (terrestrial refraction), with attention to historical sources and editorial practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of point of view in exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Place methods and theorems in as clear and general a point of view as possible so that fundamental principles (even if intuitive) are seen more plainly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author should endeavour to show that a theorem constitutes a fundamental principle of the method used and present it in a general framework; this can render intuitively difficult proofs easier to grasp. Emphasize conceptual framing rather than isolated manipulative steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing intuitive difficulty in proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge when a principle is intuitive and its proof difficult, and attempt to reduce difficulty by better positioning within general theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a principle is 'intuitive' but hard to prove, supply a viewpoint or reformulation that makes its truth clearer. Do not omit discussion about why a result is conceptually important even if the formal proof is hard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide multiple demonstrations / alternative approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Where possible, give more than one demonstration (e.g., algebraic and polar/geometric) of the same proposition to illuminate different aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply an algebraic derivation and a geometric/polar phrasing when available. State the general principle relied upon (citing sources like Salmon) and show how alternative methods lead to the same envelope/curve to strengthen understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit statement and use of general principles
rubrics_metrics.description: When using a general principle (e.g., 'line L touches curve LM = R^2'), state it explicitly and cite source or standard reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote the general principle before applying it, and show how it is instantiated in the particular demonstration (as in Salmon’s Conic Sections). This aids reproducibility and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebraic rigor and stepwise elimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Define intermediate quantities (A, B, C, etc.), perform substitutions, differentiations, and eliminations systematically to derive envelope equations and show degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For conic/envelope problems: introduce shorthand symbols for coefficients, differentiate appropriately, combine equations to eliminate differentials, equate coefficients, and show the final envelope equation and its degree explicitly (as is done deriving equation (10)). Include key intermediate equations rather than skipping steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate converses and establish equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate and prove converses of stated propositions (e.g., if polars are tangents then poles trace a conic), and show identity/equivalence of constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After proving a forward statement, attempt the converse; when two constructions are claimed reciprocal, demonstrate algebraically (compare coefficients) and geometrically (poles/polars) that they coincide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat special and indeterminate cases explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and analyze special cases (parabola, circle, axes contact, focus at origin, degenerate/indeterminate cases) rather than assuming generic position throughout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate the argument into cases (e.g., b=0, d=0, e=0; origin at focus) and show how the general equation reduces and what geometric type (ellipse, hyperbola, parabola) the envelope becomes. Discuss indeterminate cases (porismatic/degenerate) and show when constructions fail or require modification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give corollaries and geometric interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: After algebraic derivation, state corollaries and interpret results geometrically (reciprocal polars, relation of asymptotes, locus passing through origin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight geometric meaning: when the reciprocal curve is ellipse/hyperbola/parabola, relation to focus/directrix, asymptote directions, and consequences for construction. Use polar phraseology to restate algebraic results in geometric language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and generation methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide procedures to generate the curve (e.g., draw a tangent, take its pole, locus of poles is the reciprocal curve) and explicit constructions for practical generation of locus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include step-by-step geometric constructions that realize the algebraic locus and explain reciprocity: how one curve is generated from the other and vice versa, so readers can visualize and reproduce the curve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and citation of standard values/constants and tables in applied formulae
rubrics_metrics.description: When deriving applied formulas (e.g., coefficient of terrestrial refraction), adopt standard reference values (Biot, Ivory) and state the units and standard conditions (pressure, temperature) clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the standard pressure (e.g., 29.9218 in), temperature, reference refractive coefficients, and when tables (Ivory’s refractions, Dalton/Ure vapour pressures) are used. Show how to adapt to other standard conditions (e.g., 30 in and 50°F) and record log-constants for computational convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate physical effects and justify approximations in applied derivations
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for aqueous vapour, pressure and temperature dependence, expansion coefficients, and vertical variation of density/temperature; justify simplifications and estimate when neglecting small terms is permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce terms for vapor pressure and air expansion, substitute into base equations, and explicitly show which terms are dropped and why (e.g., 'a small quantity may be neglected without sensible error'). Compare model assumptions (homogeneous atmosphere) with observational evidence and adjust formulae using empirical factors or observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical calibration and recognition of variability/uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that terrestrial refractions near the horizon are variable and uncertain, and recommend reciprocal/simultaneous observations to determine mean effects for surveying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise surveyors to determine mean terrestrial refraction by reciprocal simultaneous observations and to apply these under slight modifications; justify use of mean tables only with awareness of imperfect corrections and local variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide computational aids and auxiliary tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Create and recommend constants/tables (e.g., combined logarithmic constants) to simplify repeated calculations for practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a complex factor recurs, combine logs/constants and prepare tables analogous to astronomical refraction tables to facilitate practical computation, and indicate how to switch constants when observer conditions (barometer height) fall outside table ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial and translational standards for historical mathematical texts
rubrics_metrics.description: In producing editions/translations of ancient works (Pappus, Simson), examine manuscripts carefully, remove ambiguities, include full statements of derived suggestions, and supply explanatory notes/illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good edition should contain close translations, explanatory notes, illustrative diagrams, and the analysis/composition/demonstration necessary to understand ambiguous porisms. Avoid retaining ambiguous wording of older translations (e.g., Commandine) without clarification; give full context and provenance of manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution, fairness, and historical scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: When discussing solutions and priority, cite earlier work accurately, avoid unjust imputations of plagiarism, and seek documentary evidence (manuscripts, earlier journals) before asserting originality or borrowing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide references to original publications (Repository volumes, Transactions, Opera Reliqua), compare methods fairly, and note where authors explicitly acknowledge sources. Encourage careful archival work before drawing conclusions about priority.
